gp.text: Gross profit for fiscal 2025 increased to $343.0 million compared to $312.3 million in the prior fiscal year. This growth was primarily due to a 3.4% increase in kilo volume and a 7.7% increase in average gross profit per kilo driven by favorable customer and product mix.

other_opex.text: Sales and other operating revenues increased by 22.1% to $2,481.3 million for the year ended March 31, 2025 from $2,032.5 million for the year ended March 31, 2024. This growth was driven by a 18.0% increase in average price per kilo, which was influenced by short crops in certain markets, affecting overall industry supply, and by inflation on tobacco prices. Additionally, kilo volume increased by 3.4% due to growth in Africa and Asia and accelerated shipments from Africa and North America. These increases were partially offset by lower volume from South America compared to the prior-year period due to the impact of El Niño on crop sizes.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Our annual effective income tax rate is based on our jurisdictional mix of pretax income, statutory tax rates, exchange rates, and tax planning opportunities available to us in the various jurisdictions in which we operate. Tax laws are complex, subject to change, and subject to different interpretations by the taxpayer and respective governmental taxing authorities. Significant judgment is required in determining our tax expense and in evaluating our tax positions including evaluating uncertainties under ASC 740. We record unrecognized tax benefits in multiple jurisdictions and evaluate the future potential outcomes of tax positions, based upon our interpretation of the country-specific tax law, and the likelihood of future settlement. We review our tax positions quarterly and adjust the balances as new information becomes available.

Deferred income tax assets represent amounts available to reduce income taxes payable on taxable income in future years. Such assets arise from temporary differences between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities and from net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text:
The following summarizes our working capital:

Working capital declined $20.7 million, or 5.1%, to $384.3 million as of March 31, 2025 from $405.0 million as of March 31, 2024, primarily due to reduction in inventory caused by the weather effects of El Niño resulting in shorter crops in South America and certain markets in Africa, accelerated shipments from Africa in the three months ended March 31, 2025 of the type that occurred in the prior year in the three months ended June 30, 2024, and delayed purchases in South America in the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the prior year. The reduction in inventory was partially offset by higher repayments on seasonal lines of credit and the repayment of the current portion of long-term debt for the 10.0% Notes due 2024 upon maturity.

gp.text: Gross profit decreased $4.2 million, or 6.4%, to $61.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $65.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. This decrease was mainly due to the timing of shipments in North America and customer mix in Africa, partially offset by improved pricing in Europe. These same factors led to a slight reduction in average leaf gross profit per kilo of $0.84 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to average leaf gross profit per kilo of $0.86 for the three months ended June 30, 2025.

other_opex.text: Sales and other operating revenues decreased $71.0 million, or 14.0%, to $437.8 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $508.8 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. This decrease was due to the impact of lower average sales prices primarily for leaf products in South America and Africa, and a decline in volumes sold mainly driven by the timing of shipments in North America. The current crop in North America was substantially shipped in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, whereas comparable crop shipments in the prior year occurred during the first quarter of fiscal year 2026.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text:
The following summarizes our working capital:

Working capital increased $16.4 million, or 4.4%, from June 30, 2025 to June 30, 2026. The improvement was driven by higher cash and cash equivalents resulting from the collection of trade and other receivables, net, and the receipt of cash advances from customers, together with lower outstanding borrowings on our foreign seasonal lines of credit. These improvements were partially offset by higher contract liabilities associated with our obligation to ship tobacco to certain customers at a future date.

capex.heading: Planned Capital Expenditures
capex.text: Capital spend for fiscal year 2027 includes strategic projects to drive long-term efficiencies and cost optimization at our largest operations in Africa and South America. Capital expenditures are also planned for the routine replacement of machinery and equipment, and investments in other such assets to enhance our operational effectiveness and to support our ongoing sustainability efforts. For the three months ended June 30, 2026, we incurred approximately $4.2 million in capital expenditures, and are expecting to incur an additional $34.2 million for the remainder of the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

Leaf.text: Tobacco crop production remains elevated again this season across the Southern Hemisphere origins in which we operate, resulting in lower leaf purchase prices in our key sourcing locations. Two consecutive seasons of large crops have allowed us to slow our green tobacco purchases and be more deliberate in our buying approach this season, ensuring that we source lower cost, quality tobacco that meets our customers' requirements. At June 30, 2026, total tobacco inventories, comprised of unprocessed and processed tobacco, decreased by $24.6 million, or 2.3%, when compared to June 30, 2025. Unprocessed tobacco decreased $120.3 million, or 23.4%, to $393.5 million as of June 30, 2026 from $513.9 million as of June 30, 2025, mainly due to lower purchase prices and the slower timing of our green tobacco purchases in Africa and South America. Processed tobacco increased $95.7 million, or 16.6%, to $671.6 million as of June 30, 2026 from $575.9 million as of June 30, 2025, primarily due to higher levels of carry-over inventory from the prior year crop.

Average gross profit per kilo for leaf increased by $0.14, or 17.5%, to $0.94 for three months ended September 30, 2026 from $0.80 for three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily from improved pricing and product mix in Asia.

other_opex.text: Sales and other operating revenues decreased $35.8 million, or 6.3%, to $534.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $570.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Shipment timing in Asia, along with smaller crops from certain origins within the region contributed to a 15.8% decline in leaf volumes sold. In addition, current crop shipments from Africa and South America were delayed due to shipping constraints and the slower cadence of our buying and processing this crop season, and were partially offset by higher carry-over crop sales from Africa.

nonop.text: Other income (expense), net increased $6.4 million, or 711.1%, to income of $5.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from an expense of $0.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was due to the current quarter gain of $9.1 million recognized upon the sale of our tobacco processing facility located in Araranguá, Brazil, partially offset by higher contingent losses recorded in South America for ongoing tax and legal matters.

net.text: The Company generated $4.1 million in net income attributable to Pyxus International, Inc. for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026, which included a gain on the sale of our tobacco processing facility in Araranguá, Brazil and favorable income tax expense that benefitted from lower foreign currency volatility. Sales and other operating revenues were adversely affected by the timing of shipments during the quarter, which resulted in shipment volumes being lower than the comparable period. Gross profit was down by $8.9 million, or 10.1%, over the comparable period, and gross profit as a percent of sales was 14.8% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 15.4% for the three months ended September 30, 2025, due primarily to reduced margins for processing and other revenues, which offset strong margin performance for leaf product, particularly in Asia.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text:
The following summarizes our working capital:

Working capital increased $14.1 million, or 3.8%, from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2026. The increase was due to higher trade receivables resulting from the timing of sales and customer collections near period-end, as well as reduced borrowings under our foreign seasonal lines of credit in Africa that were used to procure fewer kilos of green tobacco and at lower costs. These factors were partially offset by higher customer advances associated with our obligation to ship tobacco to certain customers at a future date.

capex.heading: Planned Capital Expenditures
capex.text: Capital spend for fiscal year 2027 includes strategic projects to drive long-term efficiencies and cost optimization at our largest operations in Africa and South America. Capital expenditures are also planned for the routine replacement of machinery and equipment, and investments in other such assets to enhance our operational effectiveness and to support our ongoing sustainability efforts. For the six months ended September 30, 2026, we incurred approximately $11.8 million in capital expenditures, and are expecting to incur an additional $26.1 million for the remainder of the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

intro.text: This Annual Report on Form 10-K (this "Annual Report") is filed by Pyxus International, Inc. (the "Company," "Pyxus," "we," "us," or "our"). Pyxus is a global agricultural company with businesses having more than 150 years of experience delivering value-added products and services to customers. The Company is a trusted provider of responsibly sourced, independently verified, sustainable, and traceable products and ingredients, principally leaf tobacco. The Company has one reportable segment for financial reporting purposes: Leaf. An All Other category is included for purposes of reconciliation of the respective balances of the Leaf segment to the consolidated financial statements. All Other revenue is primarily composed of revenue from the sale of non-tobacco agricultural products. See " Note 1.

Working capital increased $13.4 million, or 3.5%, to $397.7 million as of March 31, 2026 from $384.3 million as of March 31, 2025. The improvement in working capital reflects increased inventories and advances to tobacco suppliers, net from larger crops in Africa and South America, the timing and related impact of higher sales during the three months ended March 31, 2026 versus the same period a year ago, and an increase in cash and cash equivalents primarily from financing activities. The

increase in these current asset balances were partially offset by increased borrowings under foreign seasonal lines of credit to capture the higher crop volumes primarily in our Southern Hemisphere origins, an increase in advances from customers for future shipments of tobacco, and higher accrued expenses due to the timing of certain accruals, including an increase for accrued freight costs.

capex.heading: Planned Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We are anticipating $38.4 million in capital investments for fiscal 2027, which includes the new construction of a warehouse in South America and significant refurbishments to an existing warehouse in Africa. Both of these projects are aligned with advancing the Company's strategic initiatives to drive long-term efficiencies and cost optimization. The remainder of our expected capital spend is for the routine replacement of machinery and equipment, and investments in other such assets to enhance our operational effectiveness and to support our ongoing sustainability efforts.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

We require a significant amount of cash to service our indebtedness, and our ability to generate cash depends on many factors beyond our control.
Our ability to service our indebtedness and to fund planned capital expenditures depends on our ability to generate cash.
We rely on internally and externally hosted information technology systems and disruption, failure, or security breaches of these systems could adversely affect our business.
We rely on information technology systems, including systems hosted by third-party service providers.
Further, even under existing laws, these customers may not obtain required regulatory authorizations for some or all products manufactured by, or containing inputs supplied by, our joint venture.

The WHO, through the FCTC, has specifically issued policy options and recommendations to promote crop diversification initiatives and alternatives to growing leaf tobacco in countries whose economies depend upon tobacco production.

Despite our capabilities, the extent to which governmental actions will affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and demand for our products and services will depend on future developments, which are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted.

Our primary sources of liquidity are cash generated from operations, short-term borrowings under our foreign seasonal lines of credit, availability under our ABL Credit Facility, and cash collections from our securitized receivables.

The amount of prepayments or the amount of debt that may be repurchased, refinanced, or otherwise retired, if any, will depend on market condition, trading levels of our debt, our cash position, compliance with debt covenants, and other considerations.
These sources of income inherently rely on estimates.
